newsitem.title: CANADA: Auditor puts Quebec 1997-98 deficit at C$3.4 bln.
newsitem.headline: Auditor puts Quebec 1997-98 deficit at C$3.4 bln.

text.p: Quebec Auditor General Guy Breton said on Thursday that the 1997-1998 provincial deficit would reach C$3.4 billion, C$1.2 billion higher than projected by the provincial finance ministry.

Breton said the provincial government was not giving the right picture on its deficit and debt figures because its financial statements were not consolidated. Consolidated statements include government funds, pension liabilities and financial results for government agencies.
"Quebec is the only government in Canada that does not have consolidated financial estates (figures)," Breton said in a report.
Quebec finance ministry officials could not be reached for comment.
Breton also said the province's debt was closer to C$90 billion than the government figure of C$77 billion.
He said that Quebec's goal to reach a zero deficit in 1999-2000 was meaningless because of the unconsolidated numbers.
"A zero deficit with consolidated financial estates is not the same as a zero deficit with the government financial statements as they are now," Breton told a news conference.
